items.content: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch’s mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses “ambient listening” to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 seconds of audio your watch’s mic detected.Apple is also releasing its redesigned Health app for testing today in the iOS 27.3 developer beta, and announced expanded language support in global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese. It adds sections like a new Insights tab with summaries for heart, sleep, fitness, and other data that pop up during the day, a For You section with personalized recommendations, and health content like educational videos and articles.Apple:Live Rewind, which can help users recall what was just said in conversation. A double-press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet, so the user can catch something they may have missed or are less familiar with. Users can ask Siri about the content of the text or save it to the Siri app to revisit later.Siri Recap, which can create high-level summaries of conversations that users can review later to jog their memory. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app, allowing users to be more present and engaged in the moment.When it comes to the implications of an ambient, always-listening AI, Apple has released this Audio IntelligencePrivacy Overview (pdf) about how it plans to protect users’ privacy when their watch is listening around the clock. It goes into detail about Apple’s claims that users’ raw audio “is handled within dedicated hardware, is not saved as a file, and is not accessible to the operating system, apps, or Apple.” According to Apple, “If you use iCloud with two-factor authentication and have a device passcode, any Siri Recap summary or Live Rewind text snippet you choose to save syncs across your devices end-to-end encrypted in the Siri app.”

items.titleZh: 苹果最新 watchOS 测试版包含其全新的常开音频智能功能
items.descriptionZh:
苹果正在把 Apple Watch 的麦克风能力扩展为“音频智能”（Audio Intelligence），相关功能随 watchOS 27.3 开发者测试版开始推送。此次新增两项能力：Siri Recap 和 Live Rewind。Siri Recap 通过“环境聆听”在对话结束后自动生成对话摘要；Live Rewind 则对 Apple Watch 麦克风检测到的最近 15 秒音频生成文本转写。用户双击数字表冠即可查看此前 15 秒对话的文字片段，用于回忆刚错过或不熟悉的内容，还可以就文本内容询问 Siri，或将其保存到 Siri 应用以便之后回看。Siri Recap 开启后，Apple Intelligence 会在对话结束后自动在新 Siri 应用中生成标题和关键要点，帮助用户事后回顾，同时让用户在对话当下更专注。

这两项功能的核心思路，是把 Apple Watch 从通知和健康追踪设备进一步扩展为“短时情境记忆”和“会话辅助”工具：Live Rewind 更接近滚动缓冲式的近场语音转写，强调即时补救；Siri Recap 则是会话级摘要，强调事后回顾。苹果尚未披露转写准确率、延迟、支持机型、功耗和摘要长度等性能参数，因此目前无法与同类语音转写或会议摘要产品进行量化对比。可以明确的是，Live Rewind 的时间窗口为 15 秒，且功能依赖 Apple Intelligence 和新版 Siri 应用。

针对“始终聆听”的 AI 可能引发的隐私争议，苹果同步发布了 Audio Intelligence 隐私概览 PDF，说明其隐私保护设计。苹果称，用户原始音频在专用硬件内处理，不会保存为文件，操作系统、应用和苹果均无法访问。若用户使用开启双重认证的 iCloud 并设置设备密码，其选择保存的 Siri Recap 摘要或 Live Rewind 文本片段会在 Siri 应用中端到端加密并跨设备同步。

苹果还宣布在 iOS 27.3 开发者测试版中推出重新设计的健康应用供测试，并扩大语言支持，覆盖全球英语、简体中文、繁体中文、法语、日语、韩语、挪威语、葡萄牙语、西班牙语、土耳其语和越南语。新版健康应用新增 Insights 标签页，可在一天中弹出心脏、睡眠、健身等数据的摘要；增加 For You 个性化推荐区域；并提供教育视频和文章等健康内容。

总体来看，苹果正把生成式 AI 和语音理解能力下沉到可穿戴设备，重点不是实时公开转写，而是围绕个人记忆、会话回顾和健康洞察构建更私密的辅助体验。潜在应用场景包括会议、课堂、嘈杂环境沟通、听力辅助和跨语言交流；但常开麦克风带来的知情同意、社交接受度和合规问题仍需观察。由于目前处于开发者测试阶段，功能细节、语言支持和可用范围后续仍可能调整。

items.content: In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities, including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

items.titleZh: OpenAI称ChatGPT在搜索领域正迎头赶上谷歌
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI消费者产品负责人亚当·弗莱（Adam Fry）在周一的发布会上透露，目前通过ChatGPT进行的搜索查询量已达到谷歌搜索查询量的20%。这一表态被视为对“Ask Chat”正在部分取代“Google it”这一用户习惯变化的官方确认。弗莱解释，OpenAI将“搜索”定义为用户输入查询并触发网页搜索的行为，不包括定义术语或简单操作说明等任务；但他没有说明谷歌搜索查询量数据的来源。

20%的比例距离超越谷歌仍很遥远，但对比来看，微软CEO萨蒂亚·纳德拉在2023年谷歌反垄断审判期间曾表示，必应经过十多年努力，在搜索引擎市场的份额仅约3%。当时谷歌将AI描述为潜在颠覆者，认为ChatGPT可能对其构成 serious 竞争，如今OpenAI的表态似乎与这一判断相呼应。报道还提到，OpenAI的搜索很可能有相当一部分依赖微软必应，同时结合自有搜索索引，也有猜测称其会将部分查询路由至谷歌。

这一消息出现在搜索引擎行业持续震荡的背景下。谷歌一方面减少向第三方网站的传统推荐流量，另一方面大力投资AI工具，不仅推出AI Overview，还增加生成式AI能力，包括带可视化和图表的个性化搜索结果。与此同时，随着搜索查询越来越多地流向OpenAI等AI实验室的服务，其他公司也在投资类似的AI搜索体验，只是名称不同。OpenAI将其称为“Intelligent UI”，即在聊天机器人回复中创建可视化和交互式界面。弗莱表示：“这就是这项技术的未来方向。你是在和一个画布对话。”

与谷歌类似，OpenAI也看到了通过广告实现盈利的潜在路径，尤其是在公司可能于明年初启动IPO之际。OpenAI此前曾为广告模式辩护，弗莱对记者表示，广告并未产生持久的负面反弹。“广告没有对产品或其使用产生负面影响，”他说，并补充称“大多数人似乎并不介意产品中的广告”。OpenAI上个月宣布，将开始在ChatGPT中引入赞助产品和服务的图像，而不再像以前那样只显示公司名称、标志和产品链接。弗莱称：“广告可能已经向我们表明，我们实际上可以做得更多。”整体来看，这反映出AI搜索正在从问答工具演变为兼具搜索、交互界面和广告变现能力的平台，并对传统搜索引擎的流量入口和商业模式构成潜在影响。

items.titleZh: Randomized Caches in HW: Overheads And Limitations (RUB, Max Planck, Georgia Tech)
items.descriptionZh: 德国波鸿鲁尔大学、马克斯·普朗克安全与隐私研究所以及佐治亚理工学院的研究人员发表了题为《硬件中的随机化缓存：挑战与权衡》的研究。文章关注随机化缓存在硬件实现层面的问题：这类缓存通过混淆内存地址与缓存位置之间的映射关系，使攻击者难以利用缓存访问时间等侧信道信息推断程序行为，从而防御缓存侧信道攻击。现有方案通常主要描述缓存架构行为，对实际硬件实现中的挑战探索不足。文章因此系统讨论随机化缓存从架构设想走向可部署硬件时所面临的开销与限制，涉及安全性与面积、功耗、时序、存储和性能之间的权衡，以及随机化粒度、地址重映射机制、与多核/一致性/虚拟化环境兼容等工程问题。该研究的意义在于推动随机化缓存防御从架构层面提案转向可实际落地的硬件设计，并为云数据中心、多租户处理器、安全隔离执行环境等需要缓解缓存侧信道风险的场景提供设计参考。原文未给出具体性能参数或对比数据，重点在于揭示硬件实现中的开销与限制。

items.content: Netflix’s TV app is getting a new “AI Discover” tab where the company will show experimental, AI-powered featuresto help you find new shows and movies to watch.The first of these experiments surfaces content based around themes, like “Something Light,” “Family Movie Night,” or “Quick Watches.” When you pick a theme, Netflix will show you recommendations that match it. items.titleZh: Netflix将通过全新的“AI Discover”标签页为你呈现主题推荐
items.descriptionZh:
Netflix 正在为其电视端应用测试一个新的“AI Discover”标签页，用于展示实验性的 AI 驱动功能，帮助用户发现新的剧集和电影。该标签页会出现在顶部菜单中，目前开始在美国面向“在受支持电视上使用英语版 Netflix 的会员”逐步推出。

从产品形态看，首批实验以主题化内容发现为核心。例如“Something Light（轻松一点）”“Family Movie Night（家庭电影夜）”“Quick Watches（快速观看）”等主题；用户选择某个主题后，Netflix 会展示与该主题匹配的推荐内容。如果用户不喜欢某条推荐，可以直接告诉 Netflix，应用会记住这一反馈。这说明该功能不仅是静态分类，还包含用户偏好反馈闭环。

技术层面，Netflix 表示 AI Discover 由其“正在构建的新智能层”驱动，该智能层能够实时响应会员反馈，并持续学习。其创新点在于把主题化发现、推荐结果和用户即时反馈结合起来，使推荐系统能够根据用户在发现场景中的明确信号动态调整，而不是仅依赖传统观看历史。不过，Netflix 未公开该智能层的具体模型架构、推荐准确率、响应延迟等性能参数，也没有提供与传统推荐方式之间的量化对比数据。

应用场景上，AI Discover 主要面向电视端“找内容”的环节，适合家庭共同观看、轻量娱乐、短时观看等需求，目标是降低用户决策成本、提升内容发现效率和观看参与度。此次发布也发生在 Netflix 增长放缓、据报道用户观看时长减少，并近期裁员约 1000 人的背景下。总体来看，AI Discover 是 Netflix 将生成式/智能化推荐能力引入电视端发现体验的实验性尝试，后续能否提升用户参与度和留存，将取决于小范围测试效果及推广情况。

items.title: Windows 11 8GB RAM configurations get a performance boost
items.description: Microsoft claims that it has made drastic improvements to the performance of Windows 11 while using 8GB of RAM.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Following a resurgence of 8GB RAM laptops earlier this year, and in the wake of promises to improve Windows 11 performance using just 8GB of RAM, Microsoft has today announced what it claims are a series of performance improvements. Driven by an ongoing global PC component shortage that is forcing manufacturers to dumb down specs, the company says that with 8GB of RAM, Windows is now 20% more responsive and 40% faster when it comes to multitasking.The development shared today by Microsoft is an update to a commitment earlier this year to improve the quality and performance of Windows 11, a major bugbear of users since its launch. Microsoft says it has taken a three-pronged approach to memory optimization: making better use of memory in Windows 11 PCs, protecting interactions that need to feel instant, and ensuring key apps and Windows use less memory. While the company admits you'll be able to do more on 16GB or 32GB of RAM, it says "we're making sure you can do more, even with 8GB."The headline performance gain is a claim that Windows is now up to 20% more responsive on 8GB PCs. Likewise, multitasking is now purportedly 40% faster in Microsoft's lab tests. Of course, these are internal tests conducted in favorable conditions by Microsoft.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Microsoft says it has tuned compression for useful apps and data, and can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory, rather than moving it to storage. In practice, this should mean that apps and tabs left open should be less likely to reload when you go back to them.The claim of 20% more responsiveness specifically relates to tasks like opening Start, searching, right-clicking, opening Settings, using the Snipping Tool, and opening File Explorer. The company says it has achieved this by backing off background tasks like indexing while you're using your PC actively. Edge now reportedly opens up to 33% faster. There's also an Efficiency Mode for Microsoft Teams, which can be set to on by default, improving launch times by 20%. items.titleZh: Windows 11 8GB 内存配置性能提升
items.descriptionZh:
在全球PC组件短缺迫使厂商降低配置、8GB内存笔记本重新增多的背景下，微软宣布针对Windows 11在8GB内存设备上的性能优化。这延续了其今年早些时候改善Windows 11质量和性能的承诺。微软称，优化采取三方面措施：更高效地利用内存、保护需要即时响应的交互、降低关键应用和Windows自身的内存占用。微软承认16GB或32GB内存能带来更好体验，但强调即便在8GB设备上也要让用户“能做更多事”。

性能方面，微软声称在8GB内存PC上Windows 11响应速度最高提升20%，多任务处理速度最高提升40%。不过这些数据来自微软内部在有利条件下的实验室测试。响应速度提升主要涉及打开开始菜单、搜索、右键菜单、打开设置、使用截图工具和打开文件资源管理器等操作。微软表示，实现方式是当用户主动使用PC时减少索引等后台任务。Edge浏览器打开速度据称最高提升33%；Microsoft Teams新增可默认开启的“效率模式”，启动时间提升20%。多任务40%的提升则基于一套高负载工作流测试：依次打开20个Edge标签页、一个4K视频、大型Word、PowerPoint和Excel文件、Outlook以及文件资源管理器。

内存管理方面，微软称已优化对常用应用和数据的压缩，可在内存中多保留最多2GB的活动数据，而不是将其移至存储，从而减少用户返回已打开应用或标签页时的重新加载。微软还表示，Edge和Microsoft 365应用中的提交内存增长最多减少900MB，Word、PowerPoint、Excel和Outlook的内存占用减少360MB。第三方应用也可受益于改进后的内存管理，WhatsApp已经开始利用这些优化。

未来，微软计划让内存压缩更智能、更高效，并让Windows功能和应用共享通用组件，例如搜索和小组件共用一个Web引擎；文件资源管理器和记事本等WinUI 3应用将设计为占用更少内存、打开更快。微软还表示正与PC厂商和芯片厂商合作，减少PC为支持硬件所需保留的内存，从而为Windows留出更多可用空间。总体来看，这些优化旨在缓解低内存Windows 11设备的体验压力，尤其是在入门级笔记本和受到组件供应限制的PC市场中，但其实际效果仍需独立测试验证。

items.title: Midterm elections 2026: all the news
items.description:
The 2026 midterm elections will determine the scope of President Donald Trump’s power in his final two years in office, and signal what voters care about going into the 2028 presidential election. While this year’s races are expected to be most broadly defined by affordability issues, there are several topics impacting the tech industry that appear to be on voters’ minds.

items.title: OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours
items.description: The Grid Protectors Program applies load shedding, a technique in use since the 1970s, to data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Electricity consumption is one of the biggest concerns that residents bring up whenever a data center is proposed in their community, which is why OpenAI is taking steps to minimize its impact on the local electricity grid. According to the company, its Grid Protectors Program aims to reduce the power consumption of its data centers as local demand increases, ensuring that the grid is not overwhelmed during peak hours. Aside from ensuring that the lights remain on for everyone, it would also allow its data centers to connect to the grid and go online sooner instead of waiting for the additional power sources to come online.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible“Whether it’s heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave, families need reliable electricity. Our goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most,” OpenAI said in its blog. It also added, “Through Grid Protectors, our ambition is to make this kind of flexibility a core part of how we build and operate future campuses. That means designing facilities to reduce electricity use when needed and working with utilities to agree on how much demand can be reduced, how quickly and for how long. The arrangements will differ by location, and we will share additional commitments as they are finalized.”OpenAI is testing the program in its planned Effingham County campus in Georgia, with the company saying that it has already signed a 3.2-gigawatt agreement with Georgia Power that included 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response. This ensures that if demand jumps on the hottest days of the year, there would be enough power to accommodate the hundreds of thousands of air conditioners keeping Georgians cool. With the average American home drawing around 1,200 kilowatts, the 1,000-megawatt buffer is more than enough to power around 800,000 households — nearly 20% of the state’s homes.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This technology, called demand response, has been around for decades now, where large operators reduce their demand in response to a peak in demand from other consumers. Before automation, grid operators would manually call up industrial customers like steel mills and ask them to cut consumption to ensure the reliability of the entire grid. But with modern technologies and IoT, it can now be done automatically, allowing data centers to reduce their load in under a minute. In fact, Nvidia has already been experimenting with a similar system in the UK and has proven that it works. items.titleZh: OpenAI推出计划，在高峰时段降低AI数据中心能源需求
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI推出“电网保护者”（Grid Protectors）计划，回应数据中心选址过程中居民最关心的用电问题。随着AI数据中心规模扩大，社区担心峰值时段数据中心会挤占电网资源。该计划的核心是让OpenAI数据中心具备可调度的“需求响应”能力：在局部用电需求上升时主动降低园区用电负荷，确保电网在高峰时段不被压垮，同时让数据中心不必等待新增电源全部上线就能更快接入电网并投入运行。

技术上，需求响应并非新增发电，而是让大型用电户在系统高峰时削减负荷。过去电网运营商需要人工联系钢厂等工业用户降低用电；如今借助自动化和物联网技术，数据中心可在不到一分钟内自动降载。OpenAI表示，希望把园区灵活性变成未来数据中心设计和运营的核心部分，与公用事业公司约定可削减多少负荷、响应速度多快、可持续多久；具体安排会因地点而异，并将在最终确定后公布更多承诺。其目标是，无论北方寒潮供暖还是南方热浪空调，都能在社区最需要电力时提供可调用的灵活性资源。

OpenAI正在佐治亚州规划中的Effingham County园区测试该计划。公司已与Georgia Power签署3.2吉瓦供电协议，其中包含1,000兆瓦灵活需求响应。这意味着在夏季最热日负荷激增时，可提供足够电力缓冲，避免数十万台空调等用电受到影响；按文中口径，1,000兆瓦足以覆盖约80万户家庭，接近佐治亚州家庭总数的20%。Nvidia也已在英国试验类似系统并证明可行。该模式的意义在于把数据中心从单纯的大负荷转变为可参与电网调节的灵活资源，缓解并网瓶颈和社区阻力；但实际效果仍取决于各地公用事业协议、数据中心负载可削减程度以及快速自动控制能力。

items.title: Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available
items.description: Intel says its next-generation process technology is reaching expected performance and yield maturity.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Intel Foundry last week made available its Intel 14A process design kit (PDK) version 0.9, an important milestone in the development of this next-generation manufacturing technology. The company says that the production node is reaching performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, and the results are backed by silicon validation. Intel plans to release PDK 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027, which will validate the technology's readiness for high-volume manufacturing (HVM).Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecksLeading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and SamsungASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examinedChinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined14A PDK v0.9 is hereA process design kit contains transistor models, design rules, and other information that enables chip designers to develop products for a particular manufacturing process using electronic design automation (EDA) tools. The accuracy and quality of the PDK are crucial for modelling how chips will perform once manufactured, and the release of PDK 0.9 is particularly important because it provides customers with a representation of Intel 14A based on actual silicon measurements rather than on theoretical models or simulations. At this stage, customers can proceed with product development with greater confidence that the technology will meet their requirements when it comes to performance and power consumption. (Image credit: Intel/Tom's Hardware)Intel says that PDK 0.9 lets customers develop designs intended to enter risk production around the time the process is certified, which — provided that PDK accurately reflects the characteristics of manufactured silicon — in many cases enables chip developers to greatly reduce the number of silicon revisions between initial tapeout and mass production. Of course, availability of PDK 0.9 does not indicate that Intel 14A is ready or even close to mass production, as the company expects to validate HVM readiness only with PDK 1.0, sometime in Q1 2027. Again, this does not mean that 14A will enter mass production in early 2027, as Intel itself expects to begin mass production using its 14A process technology in 2028, following risk production for its own products in the second half of 2027.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "From a customer perspective, the PDK 0.9 gives customers the confidence to design products on Intel 14A, as the technology is reaching the industry-standard performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, supported by silicon-backed validation," said Ben Sell, corporate vice president and general manager of front-end technology development at Intel Foundry.Building on top of 18A Intel 14A builds on top of architectural foundations introduced with Intel 18A but incorporates several substantial enhancements. These include 2nd Generation RibbonFET 2 gate-all-around (GAA) transistors, PowerDirect backside power delivery (which delivers power right to the transistor source/drain regions without using intermediate connections like TSVs used by PowerVia), and Turbo Cells (high-performance standard cells designed to accelerate timing-critical paths in CPUs and GPUs), which provide chip designers with additional ways to increase performance and optimize power efficiency. Since Intel has previously outlined advantages of these technologies, the latest announcement does not provide updates regarding transistor performance, power consumption, or transistor density figures for Intel 14A. You may like Intel 14A defect density is dropping faster than the company expected Intel expects 14A to be 'within 5%' the performance of TSMC's A14 GlobalFoundries unveils 7nm-class FDX Fusion node — comes 7 years after firm abandoned FinFET Beyond improvements to transistor, power delivery, and interconnect technologies, Intel is applying manufacturing experience gained during 12 months of Intel 18A production to accelerate maturation of 14A. Specifically, the company says it has increased investments in inline defect detection, modeling, and simulation to identify potential manufacturing problems earlier in the development cycle. These initiatives are intended to improve manufacturing yields, process variability, ultimately transistor performance, and reduce production cycle times. Intel also says it has introduced several strategic initiatives to accelerate technology development, although it does not quantify their impact.New collaboration modelAnother important change concerns Intel's relationships with equipment and materials suppliers. The company says it has revised its collaboration model to involve technology development teams and external suppliers earlier in the process development cycle. The goal of such close collaborations is to address manufacturing defects and improve equipment capabilities before they become obstacles for yield improvements after the technology enters mass production. Intel also conducts regular yield summit meetings with suppliers to accelerate progress on critical development objectives.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors"This has required evolving our collaboration model with equipment and material suppliers, and earlier engagement from our [technology development] leaders with suppliers to drive improvements in defects and equipment capabilities," Sell said. (Image credit: Intel)A bonus of such early collaboration is that equipment and materials suppliers may incorporate Intel's requirements into their standard products and development roadmaps. This could give Intel an advantage over competitors, which would have to either adapt their manufacturing processes to equipment optimized around Intel's requirements or work with suppliers to develop alternative solutions from scratch.Historically, Intel frequently set the direction for semiconductor manufacturing technologies as other chipmakers subsequently adopted similar approaches. One notable exception was immersion DUV lithography, which Intel adopted after TSMC, which led the development of immersion DUV lithography. By engaging equipment and materials suppliers earlier, Intel could regain some of its historical influence over the development of industry-standard manufacturing solutions, though the importance of this should not be overestimated. What to read next Intel installs production tools at Fab 62 in Arizona, provides updates on Ohio chip fab Intel's Core Ultra 400 'Nova Lake' launch schedule leaks out Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand Expanding design ecosystemMeanwhile, Intel continues to expand the design ecosystem for its 14A technology. Cadence and Intel have established a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) collaboration focused on next-generation AI-driven design tools and intellectual property, whereas Keysight, Siemens, and Synopsys have announced design-tool certifications for the process. Intel is also working with other software developers and IP providers to validate design flows and reusable building blocks required by prospective foundry customers. (Image credit: Intel)Intel says it is encouraged by customer feedback regarding the progress of 14A development. However, the company has not identified any customers that have committed to manufacturing products using the technology, disclosed customer tape-outs, or announced specific manufacturing agreements, which is normal for the foundry industry. For Intel Foundry, attracting external customers remains particularly important because development costs of modern leading-edge process technologies can only be recoupled when they are used to make hundreds of millions of chips, way more than Intel sells these days. Meanwhile, the commercial success of Intel Foundry with advanced manufacturing technologies depends not only on transistor performance and manufacturing yields, but also on its ability to deliver predictable development schedules.Looking ahead, Intel intends to continue improving performance, yields, variability, and manufacturing cycle times of 14A, though for now the company does not disclose any actual goals. Intel also plans additional process enhancements and performance refinements for 14A-E and 14A-P nodes after the initial technology becomes available. However, exact schedules for these nodes are not known at the moment."Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027," said Ali Farhang, corporate vice president and general manager of Intel Foundry's design technology platform organization. "I am looking forward to sustaining this level of quality across future releases and continuing to earn our customers' trust by delivering on our commitments with a customer-first mindset." items.titleZh: 英特尔14A随着PDK 0.9的发布距量产更近一步
items.descriptionZh:
英特尔代工（Intel Foundry）近期发布了Intel 14A工艺设计套件（PDK）0.9版，这是其下一代先进制造工艺开发中的重要里程碑。PDK包含晶体管模型、设计规则等信息，使芯片设计人员能够借助EDA工具针对特定工艺开发产品；PDK的准确性和质量直接影响芯片流片后性能与功耗的建模精度。此次PDK 0.9的关键意义在于，它基于实际硅片测量数据，而不是理论模型或仿真结果，因此客户可以更有信心地基于Intel 14A启动产品开发，并相信该工艺在性能和功耗方面能够满足需求。英特尔表示，14A已达到这一开发阶段应有的性能和良率成熟度，并有硅验证数据支撑。

按照英特尔规划，PDK 1.0将于2027年第一季度发布，用于验证14A是否具备高量产（HVM）准备度。不过，PDK 0.9的发布并不意味着14A已经或即将进入量产。英特尔预计2027年下半年先为自有产品进行风险试产，2028年才开始14A大规模量产；PDK 1.0也不代表2027年初就会量产。英特尔代工前端技术开发 corporate vice president 兼总经理Ben Sell表示，PDK 0.9让客户有信心基于14A设计产品，因为该技术正达到行业标准的性能与良率成熟度，并得到硅数据验证。PDK 0.9还可让客户开发计划在工艺认证前后进入风险试产的设计；如果PDK能准确反映制造硅的特性，通常可显著减少从首次流片到量产之间的硅片修订次数。

技术层面，Intel 14A建立在Intel 18A的架构基础之上，但引入了多项重要增强：第二代RibbonFET 2全环绕栅极（GAA）晶体管、PowerDirect背面供电，以及Turbo Cells高性能标准单元。RibbonFET 2通过全环绕栅极改善栅极控制并利于微缩；PowerDirect将电力直接输送到晶体管源极/漏极区域，不像PowerVia那样依赖TSV等中间连接，从而有望降低供电损耗和布线拥堵；Turbo Cells则面向CPU、GPU中时序关键路径，为设计者提供提升性能和优化能效的额外手段。不过，英特尔此次并未更新14A的晶体管性能、功耗或晶体管密度具体数据，而是强调这些技术此前已披露的优势。

在制造成熟度方面，英特尔正把Intel 18A约12个月生产经验用于加速14A成熟，包括加大对在线缺陷检测、建模和仿真的投入，以便在开发周期更早阶段发现潜在制造问题，进而改善良率、工艺变异、晶体管性能并缩短生产周期。英特尔还调整了与设备和材料供应商的协作模式，让技术开发团队和外部供应商更早参与工艺开发，并定期举行良率峰会，以在量产前解决缺陷和设备能力问题。这种早期协作可能使供应商把英特尔要求纳入其标准产品和路线图，从而给英特尔带来一定优势；历史上英特尔曾多次引领半导体制造技术方向，但在浸没式DUV光刻上曾落后于台积电，因此这一影响也不宜过度夸大。

设计生态方面，英特尔继续扩展14A生态：Cadence与英特尔建立了面向下一代AI驱动设计工具和IP的设计技术协同优化（DTCO）合作；Keysight、Siemens和Synopsys宣布了针对该工艺的设计工具认证；英特尔还在与其他软件开发商和IP提供商合作，验证设计流程和可复用模块。英特尔称客户对14A开发进展的反馈令人鼓舞，但尚未披露任何承诺采用该工艺生产的客户、客户流片或具体制造协议，这在代工行业属于正常现象。对Intel Foundry而言，吸引外部客户尤其重要，因为现代领先制程的研发成本只有通过制造数亿颗芯片才能摊薄，远超英特尔当前自身销量；其先进制程的商业成功不仅取决于晶体管性能和良率，也取决于能否按可预测的开发进度交付。

展望后续，英特尔计划继续改善14A的性能、良率、工艺变异和制造周期，但目前未披露具体目标；在初始技术可用后，还计划推出14A-E和14A-P等增强版本，具体时间表尚不清楚。下一个主要里程碑是预计2027年第一季度发布的Intel 14A PDK 1.0。英特尔代工设计技术平台组织 corporate vice president 兼总经理Ali Farhang表示，公司希望在后续版本中保持质量水平，并以客户优先的心态兑现承诺、赢得客户信任。

items.title: 8 converted jet engines are powering xAI data centers as companies look for new energy sources
items.description: A Mississippi xAI data center is using eight converted jet engine turbines as a power source despite the known health risks of the carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds they produce.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk's xAI is using eight converted jet engine turbines to power a Mississippi data center. While the generators have the required state-level permission and permits, there remain concerns about the impact they could have on the local environment. The permits allow for a 25% higher limit in pollutants known as volatile organic compounds, but those compounds, paired with the expulsion of carbon monoxide, have environmentalists warning that the use of jet engines to power data centers is a step in the wrong direction. The New York Times reports that the Southern Environmental Law Center has already challenged Mississippi's decision to approve the turbines for use at xAI's data center.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe group argues that xAI has failed to provide guarantees that the jet-powered turbines meet emissions standards for specific pollutants, including formaldehyde. It also accuses xAI of what the report terms the "undercounting" of projected emissions in relation to the data center's power sources. This comes after the same group sued xAI over its use of gas generators without the required permits in an area with more than 100,000 inhabitants.The generators used by xAI are converted by ProEnergy, a Missouri-based outfit that repurposes the unused General Electric turbines that are typically found attached to Boeing airplanes. The company was quick to turn its attention to the possibility of using the jet engines to power data centers after it was identified that the demand for energy was outpacing the ability of traditional utility companies to keep up. Each turbine is capable of producing up to 50 megawatts of electricity. Normally, that would be enough to keep around 15,000 homes up and running.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The availability of energy has long been an issue for data centers, both existing and those still on the drawing board. A July 2026 report predicted that data centers would use 20% of all U.S. power by 2035, a figure that was a huge 83% increase over the same forecast that was made seven months prior. Despite that news, as of April this year, half of data center buildouts had been canceled or delayed due to, among other things, a lack of power. This is an issue for xAI especially, with Musk saying in August that xAI would increase its data center capacity by 7x before the end of 2027. Delays and cancelations have the potential to derail those plans.Public sentiment around data centers has turned sour in recent months amid power issues and concerns over how much water these facilities use. While using converted jet engines could potentially help with one issue, it seems unlikely that the pollution they generate will help assuage the concerns of locals anytime soon. items.titleZh: 8台改装喷气发动机正为xAI数据中心供电，企业纷纷寻找新能源
items.descriptionZh:
xAI正在密西西比州一处数据中心部署八台由航空发动机涡轮改装而成的发电机组，为AI数据中心供电。这些设备虽然已经获得州级许可，但环保争议正在升温。相关许可允许其挥发性有机物（VOCs）排放上限比常规提高25%；环保人士认为，这些VOCs与一氧化碳排放叠加，意味着用喷气发动机为数据中心供电是错误方向。南方环境法律中心已对密西西比州批准这些涡轮机用于xAI数据中心提出挑战，称xAI未能保证设备满足包括甲醛在内的特定污染物排放标准，并指控其低估了与数据中心电源相关的预计排放量。该组织此前还就xAI在人口超过10万的地区使用未获所需许可的燃气发电机提起诉讼。

这些机组由密苏里州公司ProEnergy改装，方式是将其通常安装在波音飞机上的闲置通用电气（GE）涡轮机重新利用，改为陆用发电设备。每台涡轮机最高可产生50兆瓦电力，八台理论总容量约为400兆瓦；单台正常足以维持约1.5万户家庭用电。其背景是数据中心能源需求增长快于传统公用事业公司的供电能力，而改装航空涡轮机可较快部署，绕过电网接入瓶颈，为AI算力扩张提供临时或离网电力。

能源可用性长期困扰数据中心。一份2026年7月的报告预测，到2035年数据中心将消耗美国全部电力的20%，比七个月前同一预测高出83%。但截至今年4月，半数数据中心建设项目因电力不足等原因被取消或延期。xAI面临的压力尤其明显：Musk曾表示，xAI将在2027年底前把数据中心容量扩大7倍，延期和取消可能打乱这一计划。与此同时，电力问题和用水担忧已使公众对数据中心的态度转差；改装喷气发动机或许能缓解供电问题，但其排放难以平息当地环保担忧。技术影响上，这一案例反映出AI基础设施扩张正与能源供给、排放监管和社区接受度发生冲突；应用场景主要是AI数据中心快速扩容、临时供电，以及电网受限地区的离网供电。

items.content: People hate data centers. They’re loud, resource-hungry eyesores that are so profoundly unpopular they have managed to achieve the near-impossible in today’s polarized political landscape: genuine bipartisan opposition. But what about “compute campuses”? Those sound lovely, right?OpenAI seems to be gambling that a quiet rebrand could be all it takes to defuse the growing political backlash that threatens to derail the infrastructure fueling the AI boom.OpenAI debuted the new terminology on Monday in an announcement launching its new “Grid Protectors Program.” The initiative, starting with an upcoming site in Effingham County, Georgia, aims to address concerns about the strain its sprawling AI infrastructure places on local power grids, particularly during extreme weather and emergencies. It’s a familiar data center problem. Yet in the roughly 900-word announcement, the term “data center” appeared just twice, outnumbered by “compute campus.”The initiative addresses worries about electricity use and the prospect of consumers being left to foot the bill for the AI buildout. OpenAI promises to “pay the costs we create” and “help communities keep the lights on.” Its two mentions of “data center” reinforce the connection: One references US data center capacity and electricity consumption, while the other directly compares OpenAI’s new “compute facilities” with “data centers built even a few years ago.” They’re “much different,” OpenAI says, with the new campuses allowing the company to be rather vaguely “flexible in our power demand.”RelatedMaine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the SenateData center backlash is uniting AmericaDemocrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edgeThe terminology appears to be new for OpenAI. A quick search of its website turned up no previous uses of the term. The timing is noteworthy, too. On Monday, Axios reported that OpenAI was planning to rebrand data centers as “AI compute campuses” as part of a policy and PR push after Tuesday’s midterms, anticipating a more hostile regulatory environment if Democrats make gains. Apparently, the rebrand couldn’t wait.Critics, however, aren’t buying it. A new name does nothing to lessen data centers’ environmental footprint, ease the burdens they place on local resources, or address the concerns of nearby residents. Activist groups who spoke to The Verge see the rebrand as a fairly transparent attempt to break free from an increasingly toxic label without meaningfully tackling what made it toxic to begin with. It fits within a broader lobbying push by Big Tech to counter souring public sentiment.“OpenAI is clearly responding to the unpopularity of data centers,” said Holly Elmore, founder and executive director of PauseAI US, a grassroots group campaigning to pause AI development.“Rebranding them ‘compute campuses’ may fool listeners once or twice but it’s not the name ‘data center’ that is unpopular — it’s the giant, polluting construction projects that apparently threatened to turn off people’s heat in the winter,” Elmore told The Verge in an email, calling OpenAI’s electricity announcement “woefully tone deaf.”“Communities that despise them will not be fooled into thinking they have transformed into something else.”RelatedVoters in Texas agree: They hate data centersYour future is in VirginiaAI backlash is coming for electionsAbre’ Conner, director of the NAACP’s Center for Environmental and Climate Justice, was similarly unimpressed. “This feels like an empty solution to an existing issue, which is that the data center infrastructure causes real harm,” she told The Verge. “Changing the name does not fix the problem and makes it seem like people’s health and our environment are public relations problems not environmental and climate concerns.”Conner argued that OpenAI should focus on changing its practices rather than what it calls data centers. “At a time when companies could utilize their resources to develop new models, create more transparency, and slow the infrastructure development, their solution is to just change their name.”Elmore agreed, suggesting the data center rebrand was an attempt by OpenAI to keep up with its rival Anthropic, but that it isn’t “spinning it nearly as well.” Earlier this year, Anthropic pledged to cover 100 percent of the upgrades needed to connect its data centers to power grids, including those that would normally be passed on to consumers. The company has also promised to invest billions of dollars in community projects developed with local leaders, protect local water supplies, and refrain from asking public officials to sign NDAs — a practice that has recently come under scrutiny. Anthropic said those commitments apply to both leased and owned data centers. Leased facilities currently make up most of its infrastructure, though its recent S-1 filing ahead of its IPO indicates the company wants to aggressively build its own, too, with many relying on gas.OpenAI did not respond to The Verge’s request for comment about its decision to change nomenclature, its motivations for doing so, or whether doing so is an attempt to distance itself from the growing controversy surrounding data centers.

items.titleZh: OpenAI悄然将数据中心更名为“计算园区”
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI正在尝试用更温和的命名来缓解外界对其AI基础设施扩张的抵触情绪。长期以来，数据中心因噪音大、耗水耗电、占用土地资源而广受批评，甚至在当前高度极化的美国政治环境中形成了罕见的跨党派反对。面对这种压力，OpenAI在周一宣布启动“Grid Protectors Program”（电网保护者计划），并开始把数据中心称为“compute campus”（算力园区）。该计划首个项目将落地佐治亚州埃芬汉县，重点是回应外界对其大规模AI基础设施给当地电网带来压力的担忧，尤其是在极端天气和紧急情况下。

从公关策略看，这次改名意味明显。OpenAI在约900字公告中仅两次使用“data center”，而“compute campus”出现次数更多。公告承诺OpenAI将“支付我们造成的成本”，并“帮助社区维持供电”。两处“数据中心”提法分别涉及美国数据中心容量与电力消耗，以及将OpenAI新的“算力设施”与“几年前建设的数据中心”对比。OpenAI称二者“非常不同”，新园区使其在电力需求上可以“灵活”安排，但公告没有给出具体容量、功率、成本分担机制或建设时间表等技术参数。

这一术语对OpenAI而言似乎是新用法，其官网此前未见相关表述。时机也值得注意：Axios周一报道称，OpenAI计划在中期选举后将数据中心重新包装为“AI算力园区”，作为政策和公关推动的一部分，以应对可能更敌对的监管环境。报道认为，这一改名行动甚至等不到选举之后。

批评者并不认可。活动人士认为，改名不会减少数据中心的环境足迹、对当地资源的压力，也不会消除附近居民的实际担忧。PauseAI US创始人兼执行主任Holly Elmore表示，OpenAI显然是在回应数据中心的不受欢迎，但“data center”之所以不受欢迎，不是因为名字，而是因为大型、污染性的建设项目，甚至可能威胁冬季供暖；她称OpenAI的电力公告“严重不合时宜”。NAACP环境与气候正义中心主任Abre’ Conner也表示，这像是对既有问题的“空洞解决方案”，改名不能修复问题，反而把公众健康和环境问题变成公关问题。她认为企业应利用资源开发新模型、提高透明度并放缓基础设施扩张，而不是只改名称。

文章还提到，Elmore认为OpenAI此举有追赶竞争对手Anthropic的意味，但执行效果不如对方。Anthropic今年承诺覆盖其数据中心接入电网所需升级的100%费用，包括通常转嫁给消费者的部分；还承诺与地方领导人共同开发社区项目、投资数十亿美元、保护当地水源，并避免要求公职人员签署保密协议。这些承诺适用于租赁和自有数据中心。Anthropic目前多数基础设施为租赁，但其IPO前S-1文件显示，公司也希望积极自建，且许多设施依赖天然气。OpenAI未回应The Verge关于改名决定、动机以及是否试图与数据中心争议保持距离的置评请求。

总体看，这不是一项芯片或计算架构技术创新，而是AI基础设施扩张中的命名、社区关系与监管沟通策略。OpenAI试图通过“算力园区”和电网保护计划降低政治阻力，但在缺乏具体技术参数、成本承担细则和环境承诺的情况下，改名难以解决数据中心选址、能耗、电网负担与社区信任等实质问题。其影响将体现在AI基础设施能否顺利落地、地方监管态度以及公众对AI产业扩张的接受度上。

items.title: Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion
items.description: Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron are facing strong demand for memory from AI data centers, prompting manufacturers to prioritize higher-margin server products and high-bandwidth memory. That shift is tightening supplies of conventional DRAM and NAND flash used in smartphones, laptops, and other consumer devices. The squeeze is also affecting smaller manufacturers, with Fairphone reporting that memory now accounts for nearly 60% of the bill of materials for some of its phones
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Apple is about to feel the squeeze from rising memory prices, with the cost of RAM climbing just as the company heads into its busiest shopping season. According to Reuters, Apple expects to pay more for memory in the December quarter, with the CEO, John Ternus, describing the current price increases as “unprecedented. The company has so far managed to soften the blow by using memory bought at lower prices, cutting costs elsewhere and raising prices on some products. However, it is reported that its manufacturing bill has climbed by $33 billion in just a few months.Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplySamsung debuts three next-generation memory technologies for AI data centersThe future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICsHigh-bandwidth memory roadmapInside the history of DRAM price-fixing lawsuitsBut that cushion is getting thinner, and Apple expects memory purchases to become even more expensive into 2027. “What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. And as we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components. Now for the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs, partly offset by a few factors. So as you know, we changed the price on many of our products, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhone in September, and these price increases provided some offset.” Ternus said during Apple’s November 2 earnings call.Memory is used across Apple's hardware lineup, so sustained price increases could affect manufacturing cost for several product categories—although Apple has not announced another round of price increases. Absorbing higher components could, however, indefinitely become difficult. Dave Nicholson, Chief Research Officer at the Futurum Group, also identified memory prices as a growing pressure point for Apple's margins and hardware pricing through the holiday season and into 2027. According to him, Apple is in a different position from companies pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into AI data center infrastructure. The impact of higher component costs is easier to quantify than the eventual returns on massive AI capital expenditure, he said.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The next pressure point for @Apple may not be AI CapEx, but the rising cost of memory across its hardware portfolio. @TheFuturumGroup Chief Research Officer @DaveN007 explained that higher memory prices could put more pressure on Apple’s margins and pricing through the holiday season and into 2027. Even with demand holding up, the question is how much of those higher costs consumers will absorb. Dave also sees Apple in a stronger position than companies committing hundreds of billions to data center infrastructure, because the impact of higher component costs is easier to quantify than the long-term returns on massive AI CapEx. ▶️ Watch Dave’s analysis of Apple’s margin outlook, memory costs, and why its AI infrastructure strategy could give the company more flexibility. #Apple #AI #Semiconductors #FuturumNovember 3, 2026And the warnings from Apple's suppliers suggest that the cost pressure is unlikely to ease quickly. Last month, Samsung, a major supplier of RAM(DRAM), NAND flash storage and OLED displays for Apple, said that memory demand would far exceed supply as AI infrastructure continues to expand. Its memory division also reported a quarter-on-quarter increase in DRAM average prices during the third quarter, while NAND prices rose by high-teen percentages. Senior executive vice president of its memory business warned the supply crunch could extend to 2028 and beyond. Elsewhere, SK Hynix delivered a similar warning, saying it had secured long-term agreements covering more than Half of its production capacity for2027 and 2028. Micron, the third major supplier for Apple aside from Samsung and SK Hynix, is also benefiting from the surging demand for memory. Its latest published outlook warns that supply shortages in memory and storage could take “considerable time” to improve.We have previously reported several signs of the pressure now confronting Apple. In January, the company was already scrambling to secure memory supplies amid strong demand, with then CEO Tim Cook warning that rising prices could have a greater impact on earnings. By June, rising component expenses had translated into higher retail prices. Apple increased prices across several Mac and iPad models, including a $400 increase to the starting price of the MacBook Pro, due to the RAM crisis. In July, Cook described the memory market as a “hundred-year-flood” and said Apple expected to pay more for memory in the September quarter. The company had also increased its inventory to $11.09 billion as it built a buffer against supply and price pressures. items.titleZh: 苹果面临前所未有的内存成本上涨，RAM价格持续飙升，制造成本攀升330亿美元
items.descriptionZh:
苹果正面临一轮由AI数据中心需求推动的内存涨价压力，且时点恰逢其年末购物旺季。苹果管理层在11月2日财报电话会上表示，12月季度的内存采购成本将更高，并将当前涨价形容为“前所未有”。公司此前通过消耗低价库存、削减其他环节成本以及提高部分产品售价来缓冲冲击，但这一缓冲正在变薄，苹果预计到2027年内存采购成本还会进一步上升。报道指出，苹果的制造成本账单在几个月内已增加330亿美元。

这轮涨价的根源在于AI基础设施扩张对DRAM内存和NAND闪存供给的挤压。AI训练和推理需要大量高带宽内存（HBM）、大容量DRAM以及用于数据集和模型检查点的高速存储，HBM通过堆叠DRAM die并配合先进封装，在单位封装内提供更高带宽和容量，但也消耗更多DRAM晶圆产能。与此同时，先进存储产线扩建周期长、资本开支高，供给短期难以快速跟进，导致AI服务器优先吸收产能，消费电子所用内存和存储供应趋紧、价格上行。苹果的iPhone、iPad、Mac等硬件产品均依赖这些内存和存储器件，因此持续涨价会推高多个产品类别的制造成本。

从苹果的应对看，公司已采取多重措施：在6月底调整Mac和iPad价格、9月调整iPhone价格，以部分抵消成本；利用此前低价采购的库存；压缩非内存组件等其他成本。此前苹果还把库存提高到110.9亿美元，以建立对供应和价格压力的缓冲。不过，苹果尚未宣布新一轮涨价，但吸收更高组件成本的能力可能越来越有限。Futurum Group首席研究官Dave Nicholson认为，内存价格将成为苹果毛利率和硬件定价在假日季及2027年的持续压力点；与投入数千亿美元建设AI数据中心基础设施的公司不同，苹果面临的组件成本上升更容易量化，而大规模AI资本开支的长期回报则更难判断。

供应商的预警也显示成本压力短期难以缓解。三星表示，随着AI基础设施持续扩张，内存需求将远超供给，其内存业务第三季度DRAM平均价格环比上涨，NAND价格涨幅达到高两位数百分比，并警告供应紧张可能延续到2028年及以后。SK海力士称已锁定覆盖2027年和2028年超过一半产能的长期协议。美光也警告内存和存储短缺可能需要“相当长时间”才能改善。此前苹果已在1月努力确保内存供应，时任CEO蒂姆·库克警告涨价可能对盈利造成更大影响；7月库克将内存市场形容为“百年一遇的洪水”。整体来看，AI数据中心对内存和存储的吞噬正在改变消费电子供应链的成本结构，苹果在假日季和未来两年可能面临毛利率承压、产品定价上调或配置策略调整等选择，而消费者能否吸收更高成本将成为关键变量。

items.title: Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims
items.description: Nvidia has told cloud providers who use its data center products that they must sell less than half of their services to Chinese companies as part of a new policy that will further impact China's ability to keep up with the global AI surge.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia has purportedly told its data center customers that they must limit the amount of business that they do with Chinese companies in what is a new policy for the U.S. company. The move would mean that data center operators who sell their services to Chinese companies must now track what proportion of their overall business they make up, limiting them to just 49% of the total and ensuring 51% are non-Chinese outfits. The FT reports the new policy has been communicated to Nvidia's customers by its sales force and regional teams, and does not appear to have been laid out in any official form via documentation.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedNotably, Nvidia's alleged new stance on Chinese customers does not only apply to data centers that are located in Asia. Instead, it applies to those based globally, and even then it only affects new and future contracts rather than any existing Nvidia hardware leasing agreements that are in place. In a statement, Nvidia notes that "American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide." The statement goes on to say that current U.S. policy "encourages" cloud providers to build on American infrastructure and to accept business from "everywhere they can."But this latest move to restrict Chinese access to Nvidia's high-performance data center hardware comes amid ongoing tensions between the United States and China with regard to AI capabilities. Nvidia can only sell its chips to whitelisted companies, a situation that has led to a thriving black market for its wares. Earlier this year, it was found that even Nvidia's older servers have become so sought-after that their values have tripled.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Whether limitations on who Nvidia can sell its chips to have had the desired effect is open to debate, with even China's state-owned telecoms giant China Telecom having recently been found to have Nvidia hardware in its data centers. The situation wouldn't be out of place in a blockbuster espionage thriller, with Nvidia CEO Jason Huang reportedly the target of a spy plot by Chinese agents.The reasons behind the U.S. government's attempts to limit China's access to Nvidia hardware are obvious. The aim is to stymie China's ability to advance its own AI technologies, with Nvidia chips the go-to option for AI servers and data centers around the globe. But this limitation on which customers cloud service providers can accept will put additional strain on companies that are already fighting it out for the same contracts. Reducing the pool of potential customers could potentially see a shrinking in the scale of data center operations moving forward. items.titleZh: 报道称，英伟达要求数据中心运营商在新的全球限制下限制与中国客户的业务往来
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达据称已向数据中心客户传达一项新的业务限制：凡向中国公司销售云服务的数据中心运营商，必须追踪中国客户在其整体业务中的占比，并将中国公司业务限制在总业务的49%以内，同时确保至少51%的业务来自非中国客户。英国《金融时报》报道称，该政策由英伟达销售团队和区域团队向客户传达，似乎并未以正式文件形式发布。值得注意的是，这一限制不仅适用于位于亚洲的数据中心，也适用于全球范围内的数据中心；并且只影响新签和未来合同，不追溯现有英伟达硬件租赁协议。

从背景看，此举发生在美国与中国围绕AI能力持续紧张的时期。美国出口管制使英伟达只能向白名单企业销售芯片，导致其产品黑市繁荣，甚至较旧服务器因供不应求而价值上涨三倍。此前还有报道称，中国国有电信运营商中国电信的数据中心内也发现了英伟达硬件。美国限制中国获取英伟达高性能数据中心硬件的目标很明确：英伟达GPU是全球AI服务器和数据中心的主流选择，限制其供应可延缓中国AI技术发展。但此次政策并非直接禁止芯片出口，而是通过约束云服务商的客户结构来间接限制中国公司获得英伟达算力，这是一种新的合规机制。

英伟达在声明中表示，“美国芯片是美国模型和应用开发者参与全球竞争的基础”，并称当前美国政策“鼓励”云提供商在美国基础设施上建设，并接受来自“各地”的业务。这一公开表态与报道中的客户比例限制形成微妙对比。技术影响方面，云服务商将需要建立客户国别追踪、收入占比核算和合同合规审计能力；49%/51%的门槛可能增加销售和法务成本，缩小潜在客户池，进而影响数据中心扩张规模。对中国AI企业而言，获取英伟达先进算力的渠道进一步收窄，可能加速转向国产AI芯片、海外第三方云服务或存量/黑市渠道。对全球AI云市场而言，算力供应链将进一步地缘政治化和碎片化，数据中心运营商在客户选择、区域布局和合同设计上面临更高不确定性。

items.title: Google reveals new Gemini 4 Carbon AI model, narrowly beating Claude Opus 5.5
items.description: Last week, Google released its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, topping intelligence rankings charts.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Last week, Google released its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, topping intelligence rankings charts. The model has landed with a grander splash than most. As Artificial Analysis highlights, Gemini 4 Carbon is now the highest-ranked AI model on its latest Intelligence Index V5 benchmark suite, beating Claude Opus 5.5 by one point. It achieves the number one score across four of the nine evaluations, and does so at a lower cost per task than other high-ranking models, like Claude Opus 5.5. Google is offering access to the model for cyber defenders first through its Fairwind program, with wider availability coming sometime after.Perhaps more crucially, Gemini 4 Carbon stands apart by topping Artificial Analysis' new AA-Omniscience v 1.1 test that tracks hallucinations and knowledgeable recall of information. As governments and institutions look to maximize value and security from their use of AI, being able to claim the lowest hallucination score could prove a significant selling point.Then again, even the best scored only 54 on the -100 to +100 scale, suggesting even the best frontier models in 2026 are a far cry from being consistently reliable when it comes to accurately recalling information.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The king is dead, long live the kingAI model rankings change fast and regularly in 2026, and it's no surprise that the latest release from a frontier lab has pushed the envelope, but Google's Gemini 4 Carbon can be seen as a comeback after languishing with irregular releases for much of the year.Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores a 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index V5 benchmark. That puts it a single point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback), and two points ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (max). It's also nine points ahead of Meta's Muse Wonder Full (Max), and 10 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback). You may like Anthropic claims popular Chinese AI model has Mythos-class hacking abilities Mistral’s new Large 4 trails some Chinese open models in independent tests OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities But raw, generalized intelligence isn't the whole picture with frontier models in 2026. As developers chase the Pareto frontier— the best-possible confluence of cost and intelligence — Gemini 4 Carbon is also impressively affordable. Its cost per task on the Intelligence Index test is actually slightly cheaper than Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), priced at $7.76 each. That's several dollars cheaper than either Claude Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, both max with fallback, and not far off half the price of Claude Fable 5.1, which costs $12.99 per task.Gemini 4 Carbon is still more expensive than OpenAI's GPT 5 Astra and about six times more expensive than GPT 6.1 Sol (max). It's about 13 times as expensive per task as the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, too, although that model measures a mere 32 on the Intelligence Index rankings. Gemini 4 Carbon isn't the best at everything, but it may be the best at most of the high price points. At least for now. Arena.ai has it holding the top spot on its Pareto Frontier chart at the more expensive end of the spectrum, but at lower price points, the Chinese open-weight models like GLM 5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4 Pro take over.Artificial Analysis also highlights that Gemini 4 Carbon isn't as good as Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at programming, and it falls behind Grok 4.7, Muse Wonder, and Kimi K3.1 Pro on knowledge work.But perhaps the most impressive score is Gemini 4's 54 on the AA-Omniscience Index, which tracks knowledge and hallucinations, beating out the competition by often significant margins. What to read next Frontier AI faces pricing reckoning as token volume explodes 25-fold China's open-weight AI models are now just 4 months behind frontier US offerings, Mozilla report claims Alibaba claims new Qwen Image 2.1 AI model beats Google Nano Banana 2.0 with minuscule 7B parameter model Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index.October 28, 2026Careful and CompliantIn Google's announcement of the new Gemini 4 model, it talked up its collaboration with the U.S. government for model screening and pre-release testing. In a similar manner to the way Anthropic handled Mythos' release in 2025, Google is rolling out access to Gemini 4 Carbon at a slower pace."We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing," Google's launch statement reads.To that end, it's opening up Carbon to a subset of "cyber defenders," and will gradually make the model more widely available through trusted partners through its Fairwind Program. Before it makes Carbon available to developers, it wants to iterate on its guardrails to make the AI safer and more effective for cybersecurity purposes, making it harder for nefarious actors to use it for exploits and hacking.Where the idea of slowing the industry and introducing greater oversight for model development has risen and fallen in the estimations of the major tech companies, it does appear to be cementing itself as more of a foundational idea for future model releases. Google talks up its release on the improved safety and security of its model, highlighting that it thwarted all attempts from the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection benchmark to have it do something it shouldn't.Google claims Carbon cuts unsupported claims in its responses twice as much as the Gemini 4 Argon model it debuted just two weeks ago. If it can't complete an action, it will just not do so, rather than fabricating an answer or hedging around missing evidence, Google claims.It also suggests Carbon will present sources and suggested actions to the user more readily, rather than pursuing its own intentions when there are discrepancies or uncertainties, allegedly cutting model overreach by 26%.As governments and companies look to make realistic use of AI, tracking usage, managing token budgets, and preventing workers from creating new exploit paths through overuse, a model's safety, security, and reliability will be paramount.Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on AA-Omniscience, the highest of any model, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48). It answers more questions correctly than Gemini 4 Argon (58% vs 48% accuracy), at the cost of a higher hallucination rate (11% vs 4%). This is still far below Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max), both at 50%October 28, 2026A new Pareto Frontier?For the past year, a clear focus from frontier and open-weight model developers has been on efficiency and cost. While raising intelligence and improving capabilities, particularly through agentic workflows, has seen great development alongside pomp and circumstance, many of the major announcements and developments have also considered cost a clear component.That's not likely to change, with the latest research from Gartner showing that just 3% of companies are actually achieving cost and productivity improvements from AI use. But as organizations push to find the real value in AI, maximize token budgets, and try to empower workers who have found improvements from using AI, they'll want consistency.Tracking return on investment with AI is notoriously difficult, with hallucinations making that far harder. If Google can sell its latest model(s) as the safest and least likely to hallucinate, and do so with high intelligence at a relatively low cost, that might be the new winning formula.At least until the next model drops.

items.titleZh: 谷歌发布全新Gemini 4 Carbon AI模型，以微弱优势击败Claude Opus 5.5
items.descriptionZh:
Google上周发布新一代AI模型Gemini 4 Carbon，发布后即登上Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index V5榜首，被视为Google在2026年模型发布节奏不规律后的一次强势回归。该模型以“高智能、较低成本、低幻觉、安全可控”的组合拳进入前沿模型竞争，而不是单纯追求单项能力第一。Google对其采取审慎的分阶段发布策略：先通过Fairwind项目向网络防御人员开放，并与美国政府合作进行预发布模型筛查和自愿测试，待护栏和安全性进一步迭代后再通过可信伙伴扩大可用范围。

性能方面，Gemini 4 Carbon（high）在Intelligence Index V5上得分59，领先Claude Opus 5.5（max with fallback）1分、OpenAI GPT-6 Astra（max）2分、Meta Muse Wonder Full（Max）9分、Claude Fable 5.1（max with fallback）10分；在九项评测中有四项排名第一。成本上，其每任务成本为7.76美元，报道称略低于Gemini 3.8 Flash（high），比Claude Opus 5.5（max）的10.04美元低约23%，约为GPT-6 Astra（max）6.25美元的1.2倍；每任务输出约123k tokens，比Claude Opus 5.5（max）的173k少29%。在相同4美元/20美元标准定价下，其每任务成本与Gemini 4 Argon的7.68美元基本持平，但智能指数高9分。横向看，它比Claude Sonnet 5.5便宜数美元，不到Claude Fable 5.1每任务12.99美元的一半；但比OpenAI GPT 5 Astra贵，约为GPT 6.1 Sol（max）的6倍、开源DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017的13倍，不过后者智能指数仅为32。Arena.ai的Pareto Frontier图显示，Carbon在较高价格端占据第一，但低价格端由中国开源模型GLM 5.3-Flash和DeepSeek V4 Pro领先。Carbon并非全能：编程能力不如Claude Code搭配Claude Opus 5.5，知识工作落后于Grok 4.7、Muse Wonder和Kimi K3.1 Pro。

最受关注的是其在Artificial Analysis新推出的AA-Omniscience v1.1测试中的表现。该测试衡量知识召回和幻觉，分数范围为-100到+100。Gemini 4 Carbon得分54，为所有模型中最高，领先Claude Opus 5.5（max）6分（48分）。但即便是最高分54，也说明2026年的前沿模型在信息准确召回上仍远未达到稳定可靠。Carbon的答题准确率为58%，高于Gemini 4 Argon的48%，但幻觉率也从4%升至11%；报道还提到Claude Opus 5.5（max）和GPT-6 Astra（max）在某项指标上均为50%，但原文未明确对应准确率还是幻觉率，反映出知识召回、准确率和幻觉控制之间仍存在取舍。总体而言，低幻觉是Carbon的重要卖点，但全行业仍有明显短板。

报道未披露Gemini 4 Carbon的模型架构和训练细节，其创新更多体现在评测表现、成本效率和部署策略上。Carbon通过更少的输出token实现较低每任务成本，在智能指数与成本之间取得较好的帕累托前沿位置；同时强化安全护栏和幻觉控制。Google称，Carbon对Gray Swan间接提示注入基准中的全部攻击尝试均成功阻止；相比两周前发布的Gemini 4 Argon，其回应中“无支持声明”减少两倍；如果无法完成某项操作，模型会选择不做，而不是编造答案或含糊其辞；在有差异或不确定性时，更倾向于向用户提供来源和建议行动，据称将模型越权行为减少26%。这些特性对政府和企业实际部署AI尤为重要，尤其是在跟踪用量、管理token预算、防止员工过度使用AI而产生新的攻击路径方面。

应用场景上，Carbon首先面向网络安全防御，适合政府机构、安全团队和企业AI代理工作流，也适合对成本敏感、需要大规模部署且重视可靠性的任务。其编程和部分知识工作并非最强，因此专门编程或知识工作场景仍可能选择Claude Opus 5.5、Grok 4.7等模型；低价格端则有中国开源模型竞争。行业背景是，开发者过去一年持续追求成本与智能的最佳组合，但Gartner数据显示仅3%的企业真正从AI获得成本和生产力改善，AI投资回报跟踪困难，幻觉进一步加剧这一难题。若Google能以相对低成本提供高智能、低幻觉和更安全可控的模型，可能形成新的竞争公式；但2026年模型排名变化很快，这一优势可能只是阶段性的。

items.title: China deploys 'world's first' 800-volt DC power system for massive AI data center
items.description: Firm says it has completed the world’s first commercial data center deployment of an integrated 800-volt DC power system.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Envision Energy says that it has completed the world’s first commercial data center deployment of an integrated 800-volt DC power system. It has been testing the Dubhe Controller, supported by its Dubhe Energy Foundation Model since August this year at its Galaxy AI data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, China. Touted as offering simpler, and more efficient power architecture, Envision’s system will also support higher computing density, says a press release. The Galaxy campus will scale to 3GW capacity according to current plans, and eventually “support up to one million AI accelerators.”Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecksLeading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and SamsungASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examinedChinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examinedCurrently, data centers rely on several power-conversion stages to achieve a usable supply from the grid. Envision’s Dubhe tech converts power directly from 10kV medium-voltage AC to an 800V DC bus to boost efficiency and slashes the size of the power conversion apparatus. It is built around three critical capabilities:Stable solid-state transformer (SST) conversion directly from 10 kV medium voltage to an 800V DC bus across operating conditions.Battery storage providing both second-scale power support and minute-scale backup.Millisecond-level coordination between SST and storage to absorb GPU load fluctuations locally. (Image credit: Envision Energy)The system includes integrated battery support for fast response to AI workload spikes and for short-term backup power. It will also support higher-density AI racks, for more computing power in the same area, says the Chinese tech firm. Moreover, Envision’s system has been designed to work well with renewable energy sources and storage. Key to the efficiency and performance on offer is the AI-driven power management provided by the Envision Dubhe controller, smartly balancing power supply and computing demand. Other benefits include a more compact footprint and a reduced requirement for copper and other cabling.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: By the firm’s own accounts the Dubhe tech system is performing well. Thus, it looks set to be instrumental to the expansion of the compute resources at the Galaxy AI data center in Ulanqab. Furthermore, Envision also intends to roll out this 800V DC tech at its Mission Gobi initiative, targetting 5GW of green AI data center capacity in desert regions by 2030. items.titleZh: 中国为大型人工智能数据中心部署“全球首个”800伏直流供电系统
items.descriptionZh:
远景能源宣称已完成全球首个商业化数据中心部署的集成式800伏直流供电系统。自今年8月起，该公司在中国内蒙古乌兰察布的Galaxy AI数据中心测试其Dubhe控制器，并由Dubhe能源基础模型提供支持。远景能源称，这套系统采用更简单、更高效的电力架构，同时支持更高的计算密度。按照当前规划，Galaxy园区将扩展至3GW容量，并最终“支持多达100万个AI加速器”。

当前数据中心通常需要多级功率转换，才能把电网电力变成可用的服务器供电。远景的Dubhe技术则直接将10kV中压交流电转换为800V直流母线，从而提高效率并大幅缩小功率转换设备的体积。该系统围绕三项关键能力构建：一是固态变压器（SST）在不同工况下稳定实现从10kV中压到800V直流母线的直接转换；二是电池储能同时提供秒级功率支撑和分钟级备用电源；三是SST与储能之间实现毫秒级协调，在本地吸收GPU负载波动。

系统还集成电池支持，可快速响应AI工作负载尖峰，并提供短时备用电力。远景表示，该系统将支持更高密度的AI机架，在相同面积内提供更多算力。此外，该系统设计上与可再生能源和储能良好协同。其效率和性能的关键在于由Dubhe控制器提供的AI驱动电源管理，可智能平衡电力供应与计算需求。其他优势包括更紧凑的占地面积，以及减少铜和其他线缆需求。

按照远景自己的说法，Dubhe技术系统运行良好，因此有望对乌兰察布Galaxy AI数据中心的算力资源扩展发挥关键作用。远景还计划在其Mission Gobi计划中推广这项800V直流技术，目标是到2030年在沙漠地区实现5GW绿色AI数据中心容量。

从技术影响看，这套方案的核心创新在于把传统数据中心从电网到芯片的多级交流/直流转换，压缩为10kV中压交流直接到800V直流母线的架构，并通过固态变压器、储能和毫秒级协调来应对AI负载的剧烈波动。原文未披露具体效率提升数字，但给出的关键参数包括10kV到800V、秒级功率支撑、分钟级备电、毫秒级协调、3GW园区容量和最多100万AI加速器。应用场景主要面向高密度AI数据中心、GPU负载波动管理、可再生能源消纳以及沙漠等绿色数据中心场景。若规模化落地，这类800V直流供电架构有望减少转换损耗、设备体积、铜缆和布线复杂度，并提升单位面积算力密度，但也仍需在实际商业运行中验证其可靠性、成本和长期稳定性。

items.title: AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China
items.description: Customs authorities only check the performance specifications of a server's processors, allowing smugglers to attach high-end memory chips to low-end processors and ship them into China.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A memory smuggler has detailed how he gets export-controlled HBM chips from South Korea into China using a loophole. According to The Information, the smuggler owns a chip design firm that build cheap, low-performing processors that fall under the U.S. and South Korea’s export controls. They are then paired with expensive HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, that, on their own, are banned for export to China. But because export control rules only look at the performance of the server processor and not at the other components attached to it, this allows the HBM chips attached inside them to slip under the radar and make their way into China.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedIt’s not a risk-free operation, though. Once the mediocre processors with high-end memory chips land in Hong Kong and are smuggled across the border into Shenzhen in the luggage of commuters that cross between the two regions daily, they end up in workshops where technicians heat up the boards to soften the solder, gingerly lift the crucial memory chips, and discard the rest of the components. Despite having a high failure rate, the high price of HBM chips makes the procedure quite lucrative.A Shenzhen-based chip broker has been making big money matching up suppliers such as the smuggler and companies that are desperate for HBM. “A year ago, a single HBM3E unit changed hands in China for several hundred dollars,” he tells the publication. “Today it’s about $4,000.” With an AI chip requiring six to eight high-end memory chips, that means the broker is raking in $24,000 to $32,000 for every AI GPU.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Chinese AI labs face this exact memory chip bottleneck when acquiring AI GPUs. While Chinese memory manufacturer CXMT has already begun risk production of HBM3E and is expected to mass produce them by the end of this year, it’s still reportedly suffering from low yield, which makes their chips expensive to produce and procure. We see this with Huawei’s Ascend 950DT, its current top-of-the-line processor that goes for about $37,000 — it offers similar pricing to Nvidia’s B200 AI GPU but only delivers half the performance of the previous-generation H100.Huawei has reportedly said that its next-generation flagship AI processor, the 960DT, would deliver a similar performance as the H100. However, since the company cannot purchase HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, and Chinese memory manufacturers do not have the capacity to supply all its chip demands, Huawei told customers that they have to find the HBM that these servers need themselves. This would further fuel the demand for these chips, increase the price and make it more lucrative for smugglers to set up similar operations. You may like Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Taiwan targets illicit AI server exports to China with five-year prison terms Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network But given that this method of moving HBM chips into China is becoming more popular, the smuggler fears that South Korean and U.S. authorities would clamp down on their operations soon. Washington has been going down hard on activities like this, and we’ve seen high-profile arrests including some Super Micro executives and the CEO of a California-based tech company. Other countries like Taiwan and Malaysia have been ramping up their anti-smuggling activities, too, so it’s probably just a matter of time before Seoul follows suit. items.titleZh: AI芯片走私者利用贸易管制漏洞，将韩国被禁HBM运入中国
items.descriptionZh:
据《The Information》报道，一名内存走私者详细披露了如何利用出口管制漏洞，将受出口管制的HBM高带宽内存芯片从韩国转运至中国。该走私者经营一家芯片设计公司，生产廉价、低性能的服务器处理器，这类处理器本身符合美国和韩国出口管制标准；随后将三星和SK海力士的高端HBM与这些处理器搭配。由于现行出口管制规则主要审查服务器处理器的性能，而不审查板上附带的其他组件，受限HBM便可随整机“低性能处理器”一起规避审查进入中国。这一做法的核心并非芯片技术创新，而是监管套利：用不受限或低受限的处理器作为载体，把单独禁止对华出口的高价值HBM隐藏在系统内部。

走私链条随后在香港展开。搭载低端处理器和高端HBM的板卡先运至香港，再由每日往返两地的通勤者以行李方式携带过境进入深圳。进入深圳后，这些板卡被送到作坊，技术人员加热电路板使焊锡软化，小心取下关键内存芯片，其余组件则被丢弃。该拆解过程失败率较高，但由于HBM价格昂贵，整体仍利润丰厚。一名深圳芯片经纪商通过撮合走私供应商与急需HBM的中国企业赚取高额差价。他透露，一年前单颗HBM3E在中国市场成交价为数百美元，如今已涨至约4000美元。由于一颗AI芯片通常需要6至8颗高端内存芯片，这意味着每块AI GPU对应的HBM转售可为经纪商带来2.4万至3.2万美元收入。

这一灰色供应链反映出中国AI产业面临的存储芯片瓶颈。中国存储厂商CXMT已开始HBM3E风险试产，预计今年底量产，但据报道良率仍然偏低，导致生产成本和采购成本高企。性能与价格对比也凸显供应受限的影响：华为当前旗舰AI处理器昇腾950DT售价约3.7万美元，价格与英伟达B200 AI GPU相近，但性能仅为上一代H100的一半。华为据称表示，下一代旗舰AI处理器960DT将达到与H100相近的性能；然而，由于无法从三星和SK海力士购买HBM，而中国存储厂商产能又不足以满足其全部芯片需求，华为已告知客户需自行寻找服务器所需HBM。这将进一步推高相关芯片需求与价格，并使走私活动更具吸引力。

从应用场景看，HBM是AI训练和推理GPU/NPU的关键组件，直接影响AI服务器的内存带宽、模型训练效率和推理吞吐。中国AI实验室在获取AI GPU时正面临这一存储芯片瓶颈，而走私HBM则成为部分供应链的灰色补充。技术影响上，这类规避行为会扭曲HBM市场价格、加剧黑市需求，并刺激中国本土HBM替代进程，但短期内国产HBM在良率和产能上仍难完全填补缺口。监管层面，走私者担心美国和韩国当局很快会加强打击。华盛顿已加大对类似活动的执法力度，出现包括Super Micro高管和一家加州科技公司CEO被捕等高调案件；台湾和马来西亚也在加强反走私行动，因此首尔很可能跟进。整体来看，该报道揭示了出口管制体系在“整机性能审查”与“组件级管制”之间的缝隙，以及AI算力竞赛下高端存储芯片灰色供应链的高利润与高风险并存局面。

history.content: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch’s mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses “ambient listening” to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 seconds of audio your watch’s mic detected.Apple is also releasing its redesigned Health app for testing today in the iOS 27.3 developer beta, and announced expanded language support in global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese. It adds sections like a new Insights tab with summaries for heart, sleep, fitness, and other data that pop up during the day, a For You section with personalized recommendations, and health content like educational videos and articles.Apple:Live Rewind, which can help users recall what was just said in conversation. A double-press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet, so the user can catch something they may have missed or are less familiar with. Users can ask Siri about the content of the text or save it to the Siri app to revisit later.Siri Recap, which can create high-level summaries of conversations that users can review later to jog their memory. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app, allowing users to be more present and engaged in the moment.When it comes to the implications of an ambient, always-listening AI, Apple has released this Audio IntelligencePrivacy Overview (pdf) about how it plans to protect users’ privacy when their watch is listening around the clock. It goes into detail about Apple’s claims that users’ raw audio “is handled within dedicated hardware, is not saved as a file, and is not accessible to the operating system, apps, or Apple.” According to Apple, “If you use iCloud with two-factor authentication and have a device passcode, any Siri Recap summary or Live Rewind text snippet you choose to save syncs across your devices end-to-end encrypted in the Siri app.”

history.titleZh: 苹果最新 watchOS 测试版包含其全新的常开音频智能功能
history.descriptionZh:
苹果正在把 Apple Watch 的麦克风能力扩展为“音频智能”（Audio Intelligence），相关功能随 watchOS 27.3 开发者测试版开始推送。此次新增两项能力：Siri Recap 和 Live Rewind。Siri Recap 通过“环境聆听”在对话结束后自动生成对话摘要；Live Rewind 则对 Apple Watch 麦克风检测到的最近 15 秒音频生成文本转写。用户双击数字表冠即可查看此前 15 秒对话的文字片段，用于回忆刚错过或不熟悉的内容，还可以就文本内容询问 Siri，或将其保存到 Siri 应用以便之后回看。Siri Recap 开启后，Apple Intelligence 会在对话结束后自动在新 Siri 应用中生成标题和关键要点，帮助用户事后回顾，同时让用户在对话当下更专注。

这两项功能的核心思路，是把 Apple Watch 从通知和健康追踪设备进一步扩展为“短时情境记忆”和“会话辅助”工具：Live Rewind 更接近滚动缓冲式的近场语音转写，强调即时补救；Siri Recap 则是会话级摘要，强调事后回顾。苹果尚未披露转写准确率、延迟、支持机型、功耗和摘要长度等性能参数，因此目前无法与同类语音转写或会议摘要产品进行量化对比。可以明确的是，Live Rewind 的时间窗口为 15 秒，且功能依赖 Apple Intelligence 和新版 Siri 应用。

针对“始终聆听”的 AI 可能引发的隐私争议，苹果同步发布了 Audio Intelligence 隐私概览 PDF，说明其隐私保护设计。苹果称，用户原始音频在专用硬件内处理，不会保存为文件，操作系统、应用和苹果均无法访问。若用户使用开启双重认证的 iCloud 并设置设备密码，其选择保存的 Siri Recap 摘要或 Live Rewind 文本片段会在 Siri 应用中端到端加密并跨设备同步。

苹果还宣布在 iOS 27.3 开发者测试版中推出重新设计的健康应用供测试，并扩大语言支持，覆盖全球英语、简体中文、繁体中文、法语、日语、韩语、挪威语、葡萄牙语、西班牙语、土耳其语和越南语。新版健康应用新增 Insights 标签页，可在一天中弹出心脏、睡眠、健身等数据的摘要；增加 For You 个性化推荐区域；并提供教育视频和文章等健康内容。

总体来看，苹果正把生成式 AI 和语音理解能力下沉到可穿戴设备，重点不是实时公开转写，而是围绕个人记忆、会话回顾和健康洞察构建更私密的辅助体验。潜在应用场景包括会议、课堂、嘈杂环境沟通、听力辅助和跨语言交流；但常开麦克风带来的知情同意、社交接受度和合规问题仍需观察。由于目前处于开发者测试阶段，功能细节、语言支持和可用范围后续仍可能调整。

history.content: In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities, including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

history.titleZh: OpenAI称ChatGPT在搜索领域正迎头赶上谷歌
history.descriptionZh:
OpenAI消费者产品负责人亚当·弗莱（Adam Fry）在周一的发布会上透露，目前通过ChatGPT进行的搜索查询量已达到谷歌搜索查询量的20%。这一表态被视为对“Ask Chat”正在部分取代“Google it”这一用户习惯变化的官方确认。弗莱解释，OpenAI将“搜索”定义为用户输入查询并触发网页搜索的行为，不包括定义术语或简单操作说明等任务；但他没有说明谷歌搜索查询量数据的来源。

20%的比例距离超越谷歌仍很遥远，但对比来看，微软CEO萨蒂亚·纳德拉在2023年谷歌反垄断审判期间曾表示，必应经过十多年努力，在搜索引擎市场的份额仅约3%。当时谷歌将AI描述为潜在颠覆者，认为ChatGPT可能对其构成 serious 竞争，如今OpenAI的表态似乎与这一判断相呼应。报道还提到，OpenAI的搜索很可能有相当一部分依赖微软必应，同时结合自有搜索索引，也有猜测称其会将部分查询路由至谷歌。

这一消息出现在搜索引擎行业持续震荡的背景下。谷歌一方面减少向第三方网站的传统推荐流量，另一方面大力投资AI工具，不仅推出AI Overview，还增加生成式AI能力，包括带可视化和图表的个性化搜索结果。与此同时，随着搜索查询越来越多地流向OpenAI等AI实验室的服务，其他公司也在投资类似的AI搜索体验，只是名称不同。OpenAI将其称为“Intelligent UI”，即在聊天机器人回复中创建可视化和交互式界面。弗莱表示：“这就是这项技术的未来方向。你是在和一个画布对话。”

与谷歌类似，OpenAI也看到了通过广告实现盈利的潜在路径，尤其是在公司可能于明年初启动IPO之际。OpenAI此前曾为广告模式辩护，弗莱对记者表示，广告并未产生持久的负面反弹。“广告没有对产品或其使用产生负面影响，”他说，并补充称“大多数人似乎并不介意产品中的广告”。OpenAI上个月宣布，将开始在ChatGPT中引入赞助产品和服务的图像，而不再像以前那样只显示公司名称、标志和产品链接。弗莱称：“广告可能已经向我们表明，我们实际上可以做得更多。”整体来看，这反映出AI搜索正在从问答工具演变为兼具搜索、交互界面和广告变现能力的平台，并对传统搜索引擎的流量入口和商业模式构成潜在影响。

history.titleZh: Randomized Caches in HW: Overheads And Limitations (RUB, Max Planck, Georgia Tech)
history.descriptionZh: 德国波鸿鲁尔大学、马克斯·普朗克安全与隐私研究所以及佐治亚理工学院的研究人员发表了题为《硬件中的随机化缓存：挑战与权衡》的研究。文章关注随机化缓存在硬件实现层面的问题：这类缓存通过混淆内存地址与缓存位置之间的映射关系，使攻击者难以利用缓存访问时间等侧信道信息推断程序行为，从而防御缓存侧信道攻击。现有方案通常主要描述缓存架构行为，对实际硬件实现中的挑战探索不足。文章因此系统讨论随机化缓存从架构设想走向可部署硬件时所面临的开销与限制，涉及安全性与面积、功耗、时序、存储和性能之间的权衡，以及随机化粒度、地址重映射机制、与多核/一致性/虚拟化环境兼容等工程问题。该研究的意义在于推动随机化缓存防御从架构层面提案转向可实际落地的硬件设计，并为云数据中心、多租户处理器、安全隔离执行环境等需要缓解缓存侧信道风险的场景提供设计参考。原文未给出具体性能参数或对比数据，重点在于揭示硬件实现中的开销与限制。
